// File: app/services/analyzer.py (python)
"""High-level orchestrator: parser -> segmenter -> NLP -> risk -> graph."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Optional

from app.core.logging import get_logger
from app.models.schemas import (
    AnalysisResult,
    Clause,
    ContractSummary,
    ContractType,
    Obligation,
    PartySide,
    RiskSeverity,
)
from app.services.parser import parse_bytes, parse_document
from app.services.segmenter import segment_clauses
from nlp.clause_classification.classifier import classify_clause
from nlp.ner.ner import (
    detect_arbitration_seat,
    detect_governing_law,
    detect_gstin_mention,
    detect_stamp_duty_mention,
    detect_tds_mention,
    extract_entities,
)
from nlp.obligation_extraction.extractor import extract_obligations_from_clause
from nlp.risk_scoring.rules import apply_rules
from nlp.risk_scoring.scorer import severity_to_score

logger = get_logger()


def analyse_path(
    file_path: str | Path,
    *,
    contract_id: str,
    contract_type: ContractType = ContractType.OTHER,
    user_role: PartySide = PartySide.CUSTOMER,
    jurisdiction: str = "India",
    enable_ocr: bool = True,
) -> AnalysisResult:
    """Full pipeline for an on-disk contract file."""
    parsed = parse_document(
        file_path,
        contract_id=contract_id,
        enable_ocr=enable_ocr,
    )
    return _analyse(
        parsed.full_text,
        contract_id=contract_id,
        title=parsed.title,
        file_name=parsed.file_name,
        warnings=parsed.warnings,
        contract_type=contract_type,
        user_role=user_role,
        jurisdiction=jurisdiction,
    )


def analyse_bytes(
    file_bytes: bytes,
    original_name: str,
    *,
    contract_id: str,
    contract_type: ContractType = ContractType.OTHER,
    user_role: PartySide = PartySide.CUSTOMER,
    jurisdiction: str = "India",
    enable_ocr: bool = True,
) -> AnalysisResult:
    parsed = parse_bytes(
        file_bytes,
        original_name,
        contract_id=contract_id,
        enable_ocr=enable_ocr,
    )
    return _analyse(
        parsed.full_text,
        contract_id=contract_id,
        title=parsed.title,
        file_name=parsed.file_name,
        warnings=parsed.warnings,
        contract_type=contract_type,
        user_role=user_role,
        jurisdiction=jurisdiction,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _analyse(
    full_text: str,
    *,
    contract_id: str,
    title: str,
    file_name: str,
    warnings: List[str],
    contract_type: ContractType,
    user_role: PartySide,
    jurisdiction: str,
) -> AnalysisResult:
    logger.info("Analysing contract {} ({} chars)", contract_id, len(full_text))

    # 1. Clause segmentation
    raw_clauses = segment_clauses(full_text, contract_id=contract_id)
    logger.info("Segmented into {} clauses", len(raw_clauses))

    # 2. Classification + NER + obligation + risk
    clauses: List[Clause] = []
    all_obligations: List[Obligation] = []

    counter = 0
    for raw in raw_clauses:
        cls = classify_clause(raw.text, heading=raw.heading)
        extraction = extract_entities(raw.text, clause_text=raw.text)
        obligations = extract_obligations_from_clause(
            raw.clause_id,
            raw.text,
            obligation_counter=counter,
        )
        counter += len(obligations)
        all_obligations.extend(obligations)

        clause = Clause(
            clause_id=raw.clause_id,
            section_number=raw.section_number,
            heading=raw.heading,
            text=raw.text,
            page_hint=raw.page_hint,
            char_start=raw.char_start,
            char_end=raw.char_end,
            clause_types=cls.labels,
            entities=extraction.entities,
        )
        clauses.append(clause)

    # 3. Summary attributes
    summary_draft = ContractSummary(
        contract_id=contract_id,
        title=title,
        file_name=file_name,
        contract_type=contract_type,
        jurisdiction=jurisdiction,
    )
    summary_draft.governing_law = detect_governing_law(full_text)
    summary_draft.arbitration_seat = detect_arbitration_seat(full_text)
    summary_draft.stamp_duty_mentioned = detect_stamp_duty_mention(full_text)
    summary_draft.tds_mentioned = detect_tds_mention(full_text)
    summary_draft.gstin_mentioned = detect_gstin_mention(full_text)
    summary_draft.parties = _detect_parties(clauses)
    summary_draft.effective_date = _first_date(clauses)
    summary_draft.clause_count = len(clauses)
    summary_draft.obligation_count = len(all_obligations)

    # 4. Risk rules -> flags
    flags = apply_rules(clauses, summary_draft)

    # 5. Annotate clauses with their own risk_score
    for cl in clauses:
        cl_flags = [f for f in flags if f.clause_id == cl.clause_id]
        if cl_flags:
            top = max(cl_flags, key=lambda f: f.score)
            cl.risk_score = top.score
            cl.risk_level = top.severity
            cl.risk_reasons = [f.name for f in cl_flags]
        else:
            cl.risk_level = RiskSeverity.LOW
            cl.risk_score = 0.0
            cl.risk_reasons = []

    # 6. Aggregate contract risk
    from nlp.risk_scoring.scorer import score_contract

    overall_score, overall_level = score_contract(clauses, flags)
    summary_draft.overall_risk_score = overall_score
    summary_draft.overall_risk_level = overall_level
    summary_draft.high_risk_clauses = sum(
        1 for c in clauses if c.risk_level in (RiskSeverity.HIGH, RiskSeverity.CRITICAL)
    )
    summary_draft.missing_clauses = [
        f.name
        for f in flags
        if f.rule_id.startswith("MISSING_CLAUSE_") or f.rule_id == "RISK_DATA_MISSING"
    ]
    summary_draft.top_risks = sorted(
        flags, key=lambda f: severity_to_score(f.severity), reverse=True,
    )[:5]

    return AnalysisResult(
        contract=summary_draft,
        clauses=clauses,
        obligations=all_obligations,
        risks=flags,
        warnings=warnings,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _detect_parties(clauses: List[Clause]) -> List[str]:
    """Detect party names using NER entities + preamble + pattern-3 fallbacks."""
    parties: List[str] = []
    section_starts = re.compile(r"^\s*\d+(\.\d+)*\s*\.?\s*[A-Z]")
    blacklist = {
        "agreement", "indemnification", "confidentiality", "between",
        "stamp duty", "force majeure", "term and renewal", "data protection",
        "intellectual property", "limitation of liability", "definitions",
        "governing law", "dispute resolution", "termination", "miscellaneous",
        "notice", "payment terms", "warranty", "service levels",
        "change control", "acceptance", "compliance", "insurance",
        "audit rights", "assignment", "non-compete", "non-solicit",
    }

    def _scan(text: str) -> List[str]:
        """Extract party candidates from a chunk of text."""
        found: List[str] = []
        if not text:
            return found
        # 1. Suffix-based extraction (most reliable for Indian companies).
        pvt_suffix = re.compile(
            r"\b((?:[A-Z][\w'.-]+\s+){0,5}(?:Pvt\.?\s*Ltd\.?|Limited|LLP|Inc\.?|Corporation|Corp\.?|LLC|PLC))\b"
        )
        noise_words = {
            "having", "with", "between", "of", "the", "and", "from", "pan",
            "cin", "gstin", "represented", "incorporated", "registered", "its",
            "their", "whose", "whereas", "recital", "by", "as", "for",
            "annexure", "annexed", "schedule", "section", "clause",
            "services", "company", "agent", "customer", "resident", "client",
            "party", "parties", "provider", "recipient",
            "january", "february", "march", "april", "may", "june", "july",
            "august", "september", "october", "november", "december",
        }
        pan_noise = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]{5}\d{4}[A-Z],?\s*(?:and\s+)?", re.IGNORECASE)
        # Also catch "DTwelve Accommodations Private Limited" style names
        # where "Private Limited" or "Pte Ltd" appears.
        generic_corp = re.compile(
            r"\b((?:[A-Z][\w'.-]+\s+){0,5}(?:Private\s+Limited|Pte\.?\s+Ltd\.?|Private\s+Ltd\.?|Ltd\.?))\b"
        )
        for pat in (pvt_suffix, generic_corp):
            for match in pat.finditer(text):
                end = match.end()
                start = match.start()
                prefix = text[:start]
                cut = max(prefix.rfind("\n"), prefix.rfind(". "), prefix.rfind(" ("), -1)
                # Walk back through tokens but stop at noise words.
                tokens_back = re.findall(r"[A-Z][\w'.-]+", text[max(0, cut + 1) : end])
                kept: List[str] = []
                for tok in reversed(tokens_back):
                    if tok.lower() in noise_words or tok.lower() in blacklist:
                        break
                    kept.append(tok)
                    if len(kept) >= 7:
                        break
                if not kept:
                    continue
                kept.reverse()
                name = " ".join(kept)
                name = pan_noise.sub("", name).strip().strip(",.;:")
                # Strip leading noise tokens like "Private Limited" that
                # bleed in from a previous match.
                while name:
                    first = name.split()[0].lower()
                    if first in {"private", "limited", "pvt", "llp", "inc", "corp",
                                  "the", "and", "of", "company", "agent", "customer"}:
                        name = " ".join(name.split()[1:]).strip()
                    else:
                        break
                if 4 <= len(name) <= 100 and name not in parties and name not in found:
                    found.append(name)
                if len(found) >= 6:
                    return found
        return found

    # 1. Scan the heading + body of the first 3 clauses (preamble often
    # appears as the heading of clause 0).
    for c in clauses[:3]:
        for chunk in ((c.heading or ""), (c.text or "")[:2000]):
            for name in _scan(chunk):
                if name not in parties:
                    parties.append(name)
            if len(parties) >= 4:
                break

    # 2. NER entities (PARTY/ORG) from the first 6 clauses.
    if len(parties) < 2:
        for c in clauses[:6]:
            for ent in c.entities:
                if ent.label not in {"PARTY", "ORG"}:
                    continue
                t = (ent.text or "").strip().strip(",.;:")
                if not t or len(t) > 80 or section_starts.match(t):
                    continue
                if t.lower() in blacklist:
                    continue
                if re.search(r"\b[A-Z][A-Za-z]+\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z]+\b", t) and t not in parties:
                    parties.append(t)
            if len(parties) >= 4:
                break

    # 3. Preamble "between X and Y" pattern (last-ditch).
    if len(parties) < 2:
        preamble_patterns = [
            re.compile(
                r"(?im)^\s*this\s+\w+\s+agreement\s*(?:\([^)]*\))?\s*is\s+(?:made|entered\s+into)?\s*"
                r"(?:on|as\s+of)?\s*[^\n]{0,40}?\n+\s*between\s+"
                r"([^\n,;]+?)\s*(?:\(|,|having)\s*"
                r".*?\s*(?:and|&)\s+"
                r"([^\n,;]+?)(?:\s*\(|\s*,|\s*having|\.|\n|$)",
                re.DOTALL,
            ),
            re.compile(
                r"(?im)between\s+([A-Z][^\n,;(]{2,80}?)\s+(?:and|&)\s+([A-Z][^\n,;(]{2,80}?)\s*(?:\(|,|\.|having|$)",
            ),
        ]
        search_text = "\n".join(
            (c.heading or "") + "\n" + (c.text or "")[:1500] for c in clauses[:2]
        )
        for pat in preamble_patterns:
            m = pat.search(search_text)
            if not m:
                continue
            for grp in (m.group(1), m.group(2)):
                name = grp.strip().strip(",.;:")
                if not name:
                    continue
                name = re.sub(r"^\s*the\s+", "", name, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
                drop = {"having", "with", "between", "and", "of", "the"}
                while name and name.split()[0].lower() in drop:
                    name = " ".join(name.split()[1:])
                while name and name.split()[-1].lower() in drop:
                    name = " ".join(name.split()[:-1])
                if 3 <= len(name) <= 80 and name not in parties:
                    parties.append(name)
            break

    # Dedupe case-insensitively, prefer the most-complete spelling.
    deduped: List[str] = []
    seen_lower: set[str] = set()
    for name in parties:
        key = name.lower().strip()
        if key in seen_lower:
            continue
        seen_lower.add(key)
        deduped.append(name)
    return deduped[:4]


def _first_date(clauses: List[Clause]) -> Optional[str]:
    """Prefer entities, then generic date search."""
    for c in clauses:
        for ent in c.entities:
            if ent.label == "DATE":
                value = ent.text.strip()
                if value and len(value) > 4:
                    return value
    generic_date_re = re.compile(
        r"\b(\d{1,2}\s+(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December|Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)\s+\d{2,4})\b",
        re.IGNORECASE,
    )
    for c in clauses[:10]:
        text = c.text or ""
        m = generic_date_re.search(text)
        if m:
            return m.group(1).strip()
    return None




// File: app/services/jobs.py (python)
"""Background job manager.

Jobs are stored in PostgreSQL; Neo4j persistence is invoked from inside the
worker function. We use FastAPI BackgroundTasks for the MVP (no Celery
required) but keep the abstraction so a Celery/Redis worker can replace it
later.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import threading
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Callable, Dict, Optional

from app.core.logging import get_logger
from app.db.postgres import upsert_job
from app.models.schemas import AnalysisResult, JobInfo, JobStatus
from app.utils.fs import unique_id

logger = get_logger()


# In-memory mirror of the job state for fast polling (DB is source of truth).
_jobs: Dict[str, JobInfo] = {}
_jobs_lock = threading.Lock()


MAX_IN_MEMORY_JOBS = 200


def create_job(contract_id: str) -> JobInfo:
    job_id = unique_id("job")
    info = JobInfo(job_id=job_id, contract_id=contract_id, status=JobStatus.QUEUED)
    with _jobs_lock:
        if len(_jobs) >= MAX_IN_MEMORY_JOBS:
            finished = sorted(
                (j for j in _jobs.values() if j.status in {JobStatus.SUCCEEDED, JobStatus.FAILED}),
                key=lambda j: j.created_at,
            )
            for old in finished[: max(1, len(_jobs) - MAX_IN_MEMORY_JOBS + 1)]:
                _jobs.pop(old.job_id, None)
        _jobs[job_id] = info
    _persist(info)
    return info


def update_job(
    job_id: str,
    *,
    status: Optional[JobStatus] = None,
    progress: Optional[float] = None,
    message: Optional[str] = None,
    result: Optional[AnalysisResult] = None,
    error: Optional[str] = None,
) -> JobInfo:
    with _jobs_lock:
        info = _jobs.get(job_id)
        if info is None:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown job: {job_id}")
        if status is not None:
            info.status = status
        if progress is not None:
            info.progress = progress
        if message is not None:
            info.message = message
        if result is not None:
            info.result = result
        if error is not None:
            info.error = error
        if status in {JobStatus.SUCCEEDED, JobStatus.FAILED}:
            info.finished_at = datetime.utcnow()
        _jobs[job_id] = info
    _persist(info)
    return info


def get_job(job_id: str) -> Optional[JobInfo]:
    with _jobs_lock:
        info = _jobs.get(job_id)
    if info:
        return info
    # Fallback to DB if in-memory state lost
    from app.db.postgres import get_job as pg_get_job

    record = pg_get_job(job_id)
    if not record:
        return None
    result = None
    if record.get("result"):
        try:
            result = AnalysisResult.model_validate(record["result"])
        except Exception:
            result = None
    return JobInfo(
        job_id=record["job_id"],
        contract_id=record["contract_id"] or "",
        status=JobStatus(record["status"]) if record["status"] else JobStatus.QUEUED,
        progress=record["progress"] or 0.0,
        message=record["message"] or None,
        result=result,
        error=record["error"] or None,
        created_at=datetime.fromisoformat(record["created_at"]) if record["created_at"] else datetime.utcnow(),
        finished_at=datetime.fromisoformat(record["finished_at"]) if record["finished_at"] else None,
    )


def list_jobs() -> list[JobInfo]:
    with _jobs_lock:
        jobs = list(_jobs.values())
    if jobs:
        return jobs
    from app.db.postgres import list_jobs as pg_list_jobs

    out: list[JobInfo] = []
    for record in pg_list_jobs():
        job = get_job(record["job_id"])
        if job is not None:
            out.append(job)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sync wrapper around an async worker
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def run_in_background(
    func: Callable[[JobInfo], AnalysisResult],
    job_id: str,
    contract_id: str,
) -> None:
    """Run the synchronous worker in a daemon thread."""
    def _runner():
        info = update_job(job_id, status=JobStatus.RUNNING, progress=0.05, message="Started")
        try:
            result = func(info)
            update_job(
                job_id,
                status=JobStatus.SUCCEEDED,
                progress=1.0,
                message="Completed",
                result=result,
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            logger.exception("Job {} failed", job_id)
            update_job(
                job_id,
                status=JobStatus.FAILED,
                progress=1.0,
                message="Failed",
                error=str(exc),
            )

    t = threading.Thread(target=_runner, name=f"job-{job_id}", daemon=True)
    t.start()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Persistence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _persist(info: JobInfo) -> None:
    payload = {
        "job_id": info.job_id,
        "contract_id": info.contract_id,
        "status": info.status.value if isinstance(info.status, JobStatus) else str(info.status),
        "progress": info.progress,
        "message": info.message or "",
        "result": info.result.model_dump(mode="json") if info.result else {},
        "error": info.error or "",
    }
    try:
        upsert_job(payload)
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning("Job {} could not be persisted: {}", info.job_id, exc)


// File: app/services/parser.py (python)
"""Document parser supporting PDF, DOCX, TXT/Markdown with OCR fallback.

The parser focuses on robustness over completeness: it must never crash on
malformed input. If a parser fails, the next strategy is attempted, and
finally we return whatever text we could salvage.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Optional

from app.core.exceptions import DocumentParseError, UnsupportedFormatError
from app.core.logging import get_logger
from app.utils.text import clean_text, split_into_paragraphs

logger = get_logger()

SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS = {".pdf", ".docx", ".txt", ".md"}

# If a page produces fewer characters than this threshold we trigger OCR.
OCR_PAGE_CHAR_THRESHOLD = 50

# Soft cap for total extracted characters (prevents pathological inputs).
MAX_TOTAL_CHARS = 2_000_000


@dataclass
class ParsedPage:
    """Represents a single page or logical chunk of a document."""

    page_number: int
    text: str
    method: str  # 'native', 'ocr', 'docx', 'text'
    char_count: int = 0


@dataclass
class ParsedDocument:
    """Structured output of the parser."""

    contract_id: str
    title: str
    file_name: str
    full_text: str
    pages: List[ParsedPage] = field(default_factory=list)
    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    warnings: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def paragraphs(self) -> List[str]:
        return split_into_paragraphs(self.full_text)

    @property
    def char_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.full_text)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Strategy dispatch
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _ext_of(path: str | Path) -> str:
    return Path(path).suffix.lower()


def parse_document(
    file_path: str | Path,
    *,
    contract_id: str,
    enable_ocr: bool = True,
) -> ParsedDocument:
    """Parse any supported file type. Returns ParsedDocument.

    Strategy order:
      PDF -> pdfplumber -> PyMuPDF -> OCR (per page)
      DOCX -> python-docx
      TXT/MD -> direct read with cleaning
    """
    p = Path(file_path)
    if not p.exists():
        raise DocumentParseError(f"File not found: {file_path}")

    ext = _ext_of(p)
    if ext not in SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS:
        raise UnsupportedFormatError(ext)

    if ext == ".pdf":
        parsed = _parse_pdf(p, contract_id=contract_id, enable_ocr=enable_ocr)
    elif ext == ".docx":
        parsed = _parse_docx(p, contract_id=contract_id)
    else:
        parsed = _parse_text(p, contract_id=contract_id)

    if not parsed.full_text.strip():
        raise DocumentParseError(
            "Document parsed but no text could be extracted. The file may be empty or corrupted."
        )

    if parsed.char_count > MAX_TOTAL_CHARS:
        parsed.warnings.append(
            f"Document exceeded the {MAX_TOTAL_CHARS:,} char safety cap; truncated."
        )
        parsed.full_text = parsed.full_text[:MAX_TOTAL_CHARS]

    logger.info(
        "Parsed {} ({} pages, {} chars, method={})",
        parsed.file_name,
        len(parsed.pages),
        parsed.char_count,
        ",".join({pg.method for pg in parsed.pages}) or "n/a",
    )
    return parsed


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PDF strategies
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _parse_pdf(path: Path, *, contract_id: str, enable_ocr: bool) -> ParsedDocument:
    pages: List[ParsedPage] = []

    # Strategy 1: pdfplumber (best for tables / digital text)
    try:
        import pdfplumber  # type: ignore

        with pdfplumber.open(str(path)) as pdf:
            for idx, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1):
                try:
                    text = page.extract_text() or ""
                except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                    logger.warning("pdfplumber failed on page {}: {}", idx, exc)
                    text = ""
                text = clean_text(text)
                method = "native"
                if len(text) < OCR_PAGE_CHAR_THRESHOLD and enable_ocr:
                    ocr_text = _ocr_pdf_page(path, idx)
                    if ocr_text:
                        text = ocr_text
                        method = "ocr"
                pages.append(ParsedPage(idx, text, method, len(text)))
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning("pdfplumber failed entirely: {} — falling back to PyMuPDF", exc)
        pages = []

    # Strategy 2: PyMuPDF if pdfplumber produced nothing
    if not pages or all(not pg.text for pg in pages):
        try:
            import fitz  # type: ignore

            doc = fitz.open(str(path))
            pages = []
            for idx, page in enumerate(doc, start=1):
                text = page.get_text("text") or ""
                text = clean_text(text)
                method = "native"
                if len(text) < OCR_PAGE_CHAR_THRESHOLD and enable_ocr:
                    ocr_text = _ocr_pdf_page(path, idx)
                    if ocr_text:
                        text = ocr_text
                        method = "ocr"
                pages.append(ParsedPage(idx, text, method, len(text)))
            doc.close()
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error("PyMuPDF failed entirely: {}", exc)

    if not pages:
        raise DocumentParseError("Unable to extract any pages from PDF.")

    full_text = "\n\n".join(pg.text for pg in pages if pg.text)
    return ParsedDocument(
        contract_id=contract_id,
        title=path.stem.replace("_", " ").title(),
        file_name=path.name,
        full_text=full_text,
        pages=pages,
        metadata={"ext": ".pdf", "page_count": len(pages)},
    )


def _ocr_pdf_page(pdf_path: Path, page_number: int) -> str:
    """Render a single page to image and run Tesseract OCR on it."""
    try:
        import fitz  # type: ignore
        import pytesseract  # type: ignore
        from PIL import Image  # type: ignore
    except ImportError:
        logger.warning("OCR libraries unavailable; skipping OCR fallback.")
        return ""

    try:
        doc = fitz.open(str(pdf_path))
        if page_number - 1 >= doc.page_count:
            doc.close()
            return ""
        page = doc[page_number - 1]
        pix = page.get_pixmap(dpi=200)
        img = Image.open(io.BytesIO(pix.tobytes("png")))
        text = pytesseract.image_to_string(img)
        doc.close()
        return clean_text(text)
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - depends on system OCR
        logger.warning("OCR failed for page {}: {}", page_number, exc)
        return ""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DOCX strategy
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _parse_docx(path: Path, *, contract_id: str) -> ParsedDocument:
    try:
        from docx import Document  # type: ignore
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover
        raise DocumentParseError(f"python-docx not installed: {exc}") from exc

    try:
        doc = Document(str(path))
    except Exception as exc:
        raise DocumentParseError(f"Failed to open DOCX: {exc}") from exc

    pages: List[ParsedPage] = []
    buffer: List[str] = []
    approx_pages: List[List[str]] = []
    char_budget = 1800  # rough chars per page

    def flush_page():
        if buffer:
            approx_pages.append(buffer.copy())
            buffer.clear()

    for para in doc.paragraphs:
        text = clean_text(para.text)
        if not text:
            continue
        if sum(len(p) for p in buffer) + len(text) > char_budget:
            flush_page()
        buffer.append(text)
    flush_page()

    for idx, page_paras in enumerate(approx_pages, start=1):
        joined = "\n\n".join(page_paras)
        pages.append(ParsedPage(idx, joined, "docx", len(joined)))

    full_text = "\n\n".join(pp.text for pp in pages if pp.text)
    title = path.stem.replace("_", " ").title()
    core = getattr(doc.core_properties, "title", None) or title

    return ParsedDocument(
        contract_id=contract_id,
        title=str(core),
        file_name=path.name,
        full_text=full_text,
        pages=pages,
        metadata={"ext": ".docx", "page_count": len(pages)},
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plain text strategy
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _parse_text(path: Path, *, contract_id: str) -> ParsedDocument:
    encodings = ["utf-8", "utf-16", "latin-1", "cp1252"]
    text: Optional[str] = None
    last_exc: Optional[Exception] = None
    for enc in encodings:
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding=enc)
            break
        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
            last_exc = exc
            continue
    if text is None:
        # last-resort binary decode
        text = path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

    cleaned = clean_text(text)
    paragraphs = split_into_paragraphs(cleaned)

    # Group paragraphs into pseudo-pages of ~1800 chars.
    pages: List[ParsedPage] = []
    char_budget = 1800
    buffer: List[str] = []
    for p in paragraphs:
        if sum(len(x) for x in buffer) + len(p) > char_budget and buffer:
            joined = "\n\n".join(buffer)
            pages.append(ParsedPage(len(pages) + 1, joined, "text", len(joined)))
            buffer = []
        buffer.append(p)
    if buffer:
        joined = "\n\n".join(buffer)
        pages.append(ParsedPage(len(pages) + 1, joined, "text", len(joined)))

    return ParsedDocument(
        contract_id=contract_id,
        title=path.stem.replace("_", " ").title(),
        file_name=path.name,
        full_text=cleaned,
        pages=pages or [ParsedPage(1, cleaned, "text", len(cleaned))],
        metadata={"ext": _ext_of(path), "page_count": len(pages)},
        warnings=([f"Used fallback encoding after {last_exc}"] if last_exc else []),
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Convenience: parse raw bytes (used by upload endpoint)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def parse_bytes(
    file_bytes: bytes,
    original_name: str,
    *,
    contract_id: str,
    enable_ocr: bool = True,
) -> ParsedDocument:
    """Persist bytes to disk, parse, and return ParsedDocument."""
    from app.utils.fs import derive_title_from_filename, save_upload

    path, derived_id = save_upload(file_bytes, original_name)
    parsed = parse_document(
        path,
        contract_id=contract_id or derived_id,
        enable_ocr=enable_ocr,
    )
    # Use the original filename for the title (not the prefixed on-disk name).
    parsed.title = derive_title_from_filename(original_name)
    parsed.file_name = original_name
    return parsed


_HEADER_FOOTER_HINTS = re.compile(
    r"(page\s*\d+\s*of\s*\d+|confidential|"
    r"draft|private\s*and\s*confidential)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def strip_headers_footers(text: str) -> str:
    """Best-effort removal of repeating headers/footers."""
    if not text:
        return ""
    lines = text.split("\n")
    kept = [ln for ln in lines if not _HEADER_FOOTER_HINTS.search(ln)]
    return "\n".join(kept).strip()


// File: app/services/segmenter.py (python)
"""Clause segmentation: split a contract into individual clauses.

Two stages:
  1. Rule-based heading detection (section numbers, capitalised headings)
  2. Sub-paragraph re-segmentation when a 'clause' is still too long.

The output is a list of `Clause` objects with char offsets relative to the
full cleaned text.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List, Optional

from app.core.logging import get_logger
from app.utils.text import (
    clean_text,
    detect_section_number,
    split_into_paragraphs,
)

logger = get_logger()


@dataclass
class Clause:
    """A logical clause extracted from a contract."""

    clause_id: str
    section_number: Optional[str]
    heading: Optional[str]
    text: str
    char_start: int
    char_end: int
    page_hint: Optional[int] = None
    tokens_estimate: int = 0
    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def length(self) -> int:
        return self.char_end - self.char_start


# A clause is considered "long" beyond this char count and will be split further.
LONG_CLAUSE_CHARS = 2500


def segment_clauses(
    text: str,
    *,
    contract_id: str,
    long_threshold: int = LONG_CLAUSE_CHARS,
) -> List[Clause]:
    """Split the full contract text into a list of Clauses.

    Strategy:
      * Group paragraphs into clauses based on numbered/heading lines.
      * If a clause exceeds long_threshold, fall back to per-paragraph chunks.
    """
    if not text:
        return []

    cleaned = clean_text(text)
    if not cleaned:
        return []

    paragraphs = split_into_paragraphs(cleaned)
    if not paragraphs:
        return []

    raw_blocks = _group_paragraphs_into_clauses(paragraphs)

    clauses: List[Clause] = []
    cursor = 0
    for idx, (heading, section_num, body) in enumerate(raw_blocks, start=1):
        full_text = body if not heading else f"{heading}\n\n{body}"
        # Find char offsets relative to the entire cleaned text.
        start = cleaned.find(full_text[:120], cursor)
        if start == -1:
            start = cursor
        end = start + len(full_text)
        cursor = end

        if len(full_text) > long_threshold:
            # Split long clause into multiple sub-clauses.
            sub_clauses = _split_long_clause(
                body,
                base_id=f"{contract_id}_c{idx:03d}",
                section_number=section_num,
                heading=heading,
                char_start=start,
                long_threshold=long_threshold,
            )
            for sc in sub_clauses:
                sc.metadata.setdefault("parent_index", idx)
            clauses.extend(sub_clauses)
        else:
            clauses.append(
                Clause(
                    clause_id=f"{contract_id}_c{idx:03d}",
                    section_number=section_num,
                    heading=heading,
                    text=full_text.strip(),
                    char_start=start,
                    char_end=start + len(full_text.strip()),
                    tokens_estimate=_estimate_tokens(full_text),
                )
            )

    logger.info("Segmented {} clauses (long_threshold={})", len(clauses), long_threshold)
    return clauses


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Internals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _group_paragraphs_into_clauses(paragraphs: List[str]) -> List[tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str], str]]:
    """Group paragraphs into (heading, section_number, body) tuples.

    Algorithm:
      1. Normalise: split any paragraph that starts with a heading line and
         has a body on subsequent lines.
      2. Walk through the items. Each time we see a strong-heading line
         (starts with a section number OR is an ALL-CAPS legal title),
         flush the current buffer as one (heading, body) pair.
      3. The first item is special: even if it doesn't match a heading
         pattern, we treat it as the preamble's heading so all the
         metadata that follows it stays attached as the preamble body.
    """
    grouped: List[tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str], str]] = []
    buffer: List[str] = []

    def _trim_heading(h: str) -> Optional[str]:
        if not h:
            return None
        first_line = h.split("\n", 1)[0].strip()
        if not first_line:
            return None
        if len(first_line) > 200:
            return None
        return first_line

    def flush():
        if not buffer:
            return
        heading_raw = buffer[0]
        heading = _trim_heading(heading_raw)
        body = "\n\n".join(buffer[1:]) if len(buffer) > 1 else ""
        section_num = (
            detect_section_number(heading.split("\n", 1)[0]) if heading else None
        )
        grouped.append((heading, section_num, body))
        buffer.clear()

    # Normalise: a heading + body joined by a single newline should be split.
    normalised: List[str] = []
    for p in paragraphs:
        lines = p.split("\n")
        first = lines[0].strip()
        rest = "\n".join(lines[1:]).strip()
        if _looks_like_heading_line(first) and rest:
            normalised.append(first)
            normalised.append(rest)
        else:
            normalised.append(p)

    for idx, para in enumerate(normalised):
        first_line = para.split("\n", 1)[0].strip()
        # Strong heading only — not every numbered body paragraph.
        is_strong_heading = _looks_like_heading_line(first_line)
        if idx == 0 and not buffer:
            # Force-start the first group with whatever we see.
            buffer.append(para)
        elif is_strong_heading:
            flush()
            buffer.append(para)
        else:
            buffer.append(para)
    flush()

    if not grouped:
        grouped = [(None, None, p) for p in paragraphs]

    return grouped


def _looks_like_heading_line(line: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if a single line looks like a clause heading.

    Heuristic is intentionally strict to avoid false positives on body text.
    A line qualifies only if it has either a section number or it is short,
    ALL-CAPS and has no terminal punctuation.
    """
    if not line:
        return False
    if len(line) > 120:
        return False
    # Section number ("1.", "1.1", "(a)", "Article 5", etc.). Numbered body
    # sentences also match this regex, so reject terminal punctuation and
    # long lines; those are clause text, not headings.
    if detect_section_number(line):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped.endswith((".", ",", ";", ":")):
            return False
        return len(stripped.split()) <= 12
    stripped = line.strip()
    # Strip out parenthetical / quoted segments before checking case so
    # 'RESIDENT ACCOMMODATION SERVICE AGREEMENT ("Agreement")' is treated as
    # an all-caps heading.
    cleaned = re.sub(r"\([^)]*\)", "", stripped)
    cleaned = re.sub(r'"[^"]*"', "", cleaned)
    cleaned = re.sub(r"'[^']*'", "", cleaned).strip()
    has_alpha = any(c.isalpha() for c in cleaned)
    if (
        has_alpha
        and cleaned == cleaned.upper()
        and len(stripped) <= 120
        and not stripped.endswith(".")
        and not stripped.endswith(",")
    ):
        return True
    # Keyword hint — only if the line is very short (<= 60 chars) and is title-cased.
    if (
        len(stripped) <= 60
        and not stripped.endswith(".")
        and not stripped.endswith(",")
        and not any(c.isdigit() for c in stripped)
        and stripped == stripped.title()
        and any(t in stripped.lower() for t in _HEADING_HINTS)
    ):
        return True
    return False


_HEADING_HINTS = (
    "indemnif",
    "liability",

def _split_long_clause(
    body: str,
    *,
    base_id: str,
    section_number: Optional[str],
    heading: Optional[str],
    char_start: int,
    long_threshold: int = LONG_CLAUSE_CHARS,
) -> List[Clause]:
    """Split a clause body into smaller pieces at paragraph or sentence
    boundaries.

    Three-stage strategy:
      1. Group paragraphs into chunks <= long_threshold.
      2. If a single paragraph is still larger than the threshold, split it
         by sentence boundaries (`.!?`).
      3. As a last resort, perform a fixed-character split.
    """
    paragraphs = split_into_paragraphs(body)
    clauses: List[Clause] = []
    buffer: List[str] = []
    buffer_len = 0
    sub_idx = 1

    def flush():
        nonlocal sub_idx, buffer_len
        if not buffer:
            return
        joined = "\n\n".join(buffer).strip()
        clause_id = f"{base_id}_s{sub_idx:02d}"
        prior_len = sum(len(c.text) + 2 for c in clauses)
        local_start = char_start + prior_len
        clauses.append(
            Clause(
                clause_id=clause_id,
                section_number=section_number,
                heading=heading,
                text=joined,
                char_start=local_start,
                char_end=local_start + len(joined),
                tokens_estimate=_estimate_tokens(joined),
                metadata={"split": True, "sub_index": sub_idx},
            )
        )
        sub_idx += 1
        buffer.clear()
        buffer_len = 0

    def _split_oversized_paragraph(p: str) -> List[str]:
        """Split a single oversized paragraph into sentence-sized chunks."""
        if len(p) <= long_threshold:
            return [p]
        # Stage 2: sentence split
        sentence_chunks = [s for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", p) if s.strip()]
        # Stage 3: fixed-char split if a sentence alone exceeds threshold
        out: List[str] = []
        for s in sentence_chunks:
            if len(s) <= long_threshold:
                out.append(s)
                continue
            for i in range(0, len(s), long_threshold):
                out.append(s[i : i + long_threshold])
        return out or [p]

    expanded: List[str] = []
    for p in paragraphs:
        if len(p) > long_threshold:
            expanded.extend(_split_oversized_paragraph(p))
        else:
            expanded.append(p)

    for p in expanded:
        if buffer_len + len(p) > long_threshold and buffer:
            flush()
        buffer.append(p)
        buffer_len += len(p)
    flush()
    return clauses


_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\S+")


def _estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """Rough token estimate (avg 4 chars per token for English)."""
    return max(1, len(text) // 4)

// File: nlp/clause_classification/classifier_ml.py (python)
"""DeBERTa-v3 clause classifier wrapper.

This module is imported lazily — only if the heavy ML deps are installed.
It provides a `classify_with_deberta(text)` function that returns a
ClassificationResult with model confidence.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List, Optional

from nlp.clause_classification.classifier import CLAUSE_RULES, ClassificationResult

try:  # pragma: no cover - optional
    from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoTokenizer  # type: ignore
    _TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE = True
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
    _TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE = False


_MODEL = None
_TOKENIZER = None
_LABEL_MAP: Optional[List[str]] = None


def _load_model():  # pragma: no cover - large download
    """Lazy-load the DeBERTa classifier once per process."""
    global _MODEL, _TOKENIZER, _LABEL_MAP
    if _MODEL is not None:
        return
    from app.core.config import get_settings

    settings = get_settings()
    model_name = settings.clause_model
    _TOKENIZER = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir=settings.hf_home)
    _MODEL = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        cache_dir=settings.hf_home,
        num_labels=len(CLAUSE_RULES),
        ignore_mismatched_sizes=True,
    )
    _MODEL.eval()
    _LABEL_MAP = list(CLAUSE_RULES.keys())


def classify_with_deberta(text: str, *, top_k: int = 3) -> Optional[ClassificationResult]:
    """Run zero-shot / fine-tuned DeBERTa classification. Returns None on failure."""
    if not _TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE:
        return None
    if not text or not text.strip():
        return None
    try:
        _load_model()
    except Exception:
        return None

    try:  # pragma: no cover - inference
        import torch
        inputs = _TOKENIZER(
            text,
            return_tensors="pt",
            truncation=True,
            max_length=512,
            padding=True,
        )
        with torch.no_grad():
            logits = _MODEL(**inputs).logits
        probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)[0].cpu().tolist()
        ranked = sorted(enumerate(probs), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:top_k]
        labels = [_LABEL_MAP[i] for i, _ in ranked if _LABEL_MAP]
        confidence = float(ranked[0][1]) if ranked else 0.0
        return ClassificationResult(labels=labels, confidence=round(confidence, 3), method="ml")
    except Exception:
        return None

"""Clause classifier — rule-based with TF-IDF ML fallback.

This module exposes a single entry-point :func:`classify_clause` that:

  1. Tries the rule-based classifier (fast, deterministic, debuggable).
  2. Falls back to a TF-IDF + Logistic Regression model trained on
     real CUAD gold data if a trained model artefact exists at
     ``models/tfidf_classifier.joblib``.

The CUAD-derived keyword bank is auto-loaded on import from
``data/processed/cuad_keyword_bank.json`` to enrich the rule matcher.
Run ``python scripts/build_training_data.py`` once to materialise it.

@dataclass
class ClassificationResult:
    labels: List[str]
    confidence: float
    method: str  # 'rule' or 'ml'


def classify_clause(
    text: str,
    *,
    heading: Optional[str] = None,
    rule_based_only: bool = False,
) -> ClassificationResult:
    """Multi-label clause classification.

    Strategy: hybrid. We always run the rule-based classifier (it captures
    Indian-specific categories that the CUAD-trained ML model has never
    seen). We then run the TF-IDF ML classifier if available. Final labels
    are the union, ranked by TF-IDF confidence for ML labels and score
    weight for rule-based labels.
    """
    if not text and not heading:
        return ClassificationResult(labels=[], confidence=0.0, method="rule")

    rule_result = _rule_classify(text=text, heading=heading)
    rule_labels = list(rule_result.labels)

    if rule_based_only:
        return rule_result

    ml_result = _classify_with_tfidf(text)
    if not ml_result or not ml_result.labels:
        return rule_result

    # Hybrid: union of ML + rule labels with dedup, ML first.
    seen = set()
    merged: List[str] = []
    for label in ml_result.labels:
        if label not in seen:
            seen.add(label)
            merged.append(label)
    for label in rule_labels:
        if label not in seen:
            seen.add(label)
            merged.append(label)
    # Cap at 5 labels.
    merged = merged[:5]
    confidence = max(rule_result.confidence, ml_result.confidence)
    method = "hybrid" if rule_labels and ml_result.labels != rule_labels else ml_result.method
    return ClassificationResult(labels=merged, confidence=round(confidence, 3), method=method)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CUAD keyword bank auto-loader
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_cuad_keyword_bank: Optional[Dict[str, List[str]]] = None


def load_cuad_keyword_bank(path: Optional[Path] = None, *, max_keywords_per_category: int = 80) -> int:
    """Load CUAD-derived keywords into CLAUSE_RULES.

    Each CUAD span is a sentence-sized string. We extract short, distinctive
    sub-phrases (3-7 tokens) so the matcher stays discriminative and fast.
    A category-wide cap prevents the bank from flooding the rule list with
    near-duplicates.
    """
    global _cuad_keyword_bank
    if path is None:
        path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "data" / "processed" / "cuad_keyword_bank.json"
    if not Path(path).exists():
        _compile_keyword_patterns()
        return 0
    with Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        bank = json.load(fh)
    _cuad_keyword_bank = bank

    STOPWORDS = {
        "the", "a", "an", "of", "in", "on", "at", "to", "for", "and",
        "or", "by", "with", "from", "as", "is", "are", "be", "this",
        "that", "these", "those", "shall", "may", "will", "would",
        "any", "all", "such", "its", "their", "his", "her", "if",
        "when", "where", "while", "during", "including", "include",
        "without", "otherwise", "hereunder", "pursuant",
    }

    added = 0
    for cuad_label, samples in bank.items():
        target = CUAD_TO_INTERNAL.get(cuad_label)
        if not target:
            continue
        existing = set(CLAUSE_RULES.get(target, []))
        per_category_added = 0
        for sample in samples[:150]:
            if per_category_added >= max_keywords_per_category:
                break
            lowered = sample.strip().lower()
            if not lowered or len(lowered) < 10:
                continue
            tokens = re.findall(r"[a-z0-9'/-]+", lowered)
            tokens = [t for t in tokens if t not in STOPWORDS and len(t) > 1]
            if len(tokens) < 3:
                continue
            # Use the last 5-7 tokens — they tend to carry the most informative
            # legal phrasing (e.g. "subject to the laws of the state of new york").
            for n in (6, 5, 4):
                if len(tokens) >= n:
                    phrase = " ".join(tokens[-n:])
                    if 12 <= len(phrase) <= 60 and phrase not in existing:
                        CLAUSE_RULES.setdefault(target, []).append(phrase)
                        existing.add(phrase)
                        added += 1
                        per_category_added += 1
                        break
    _compile_keyword_patterns()
    return added


_KEYWORD_PATTERNS: Dict[str, re.Pattern] = {}


def _compile_keyword_patterns() -> None:
    """Compile letter-boundary regexes so `term` never matches `terminate`."""
    global _KEYWORD_PATTERNS
    patterns: Dict[str, re.Pattern] = {}
    for keywords in CLAUSE_RULES.values():
        for raw in keywords:
            kw = raw.strip().lower()
            if not kw or kw in patterns:
                continue
            patterns[kw] = re.compile(rf"(?<![a-z0-9]){re.escape(kw)}(?![a-z0-9])")
    _KEYWORD_PATTERNS = patterns


# Auto-load on import (silent skip if bank file is missing).
try:
    load_cuad_keyword_bank()
except Exception:
    _compile_keyword_patterns()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TF-IDF ML classifier (lazy-loaded)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_TFIDF_MODEL = None
_TFIDF_MODEL_LOADED = False


def _classify_with_tfidf(text: str) -> Optional[ClassificationResult]:
    global _TFIDF_MODEL, _TFIDF_MODEL_LOADED
    from nlp.clause_classification.tfidf_model import ensure_model_file, load_trained

    if ensure_model_file() is None:
        return None
    if not _TFIDF_MODEL_LOADED:
        try:
            _TFIDF_MODEL = load_trained()
        except Exception:
            _TFIDF_MODEL = None
        _TFIDF_MODEL_LOADED = True
    if _TFIDF_MODEL is None:
        return None
    if not text or not text.strip():
        return None
    try:
        labels = _TFIDF_MODEL.predict_one(text)
        if not labels:
            return None
        # Confidence approx — top probability of the predicted class.
        proba = _TFIDF_MODEL.pipeline.predict_proba([text])[0]
        top_idx = proba.argmax()
        confidence = float(proba[top_idx])
        return ClassificationResult(labels=labels, confidence=round(confidence, 3), method="tfidf")
    except Exception:
        return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rule-based engine
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _rule_classify(text: str, heading: Optional[str] = None) -> ClassificationResult:
    lowered = (text or "").lower()
    heading_low = (heading or "").lower().strip()
    scores: Dict[str, float] = {}

    if heading_low:
        for k, v in HEADING_HINTS.items():
            if k in heading_low:
                scores[v] = scores.get(v, 0.0) + 5.0

    for label, keywords in CLAUSE_RULES.items():
        for kw in keywords:
            pattern = _KEYWORD_PATTERNS.get(kw.strip().lower())
            if pattern is not None and pattern.search(lowered):
                # Long phrases are more discriminative.
                weight = 1.0 + min(2.0, len(kw) / 20.0)
                scores[label] = scores.get(label, 0.0) + weight

    if not scores:
        return ClassificationResult(labels=["Miscellaneous"], confidence=0.3, method="rule")

    sorted_labels = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))
    top_score = sorted_labels[0][1]
    total = sum(scores.values()) or 1
    confidence = min(0.95, 0.4 + (top_score / max(8, total)))

    threshold = max(1.0, top_score * 0.4)
    labels = [lbl for lbl, sc in sorted_labels if sc >= threshold][:5]
    return ClassificationResult(labels=labels, confidence=round(confidence, 2), method="rule")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Convenience: classify a list of clauses
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def classify_clauses(clauses: List[Dict]) -> List[Dict]:
    """Decorate each clause dict with `clause_types` and `confidence`."""
    for cl in clauses:
        result = classify_clause(
            cl.get("text", ""),
            heading=cl.get("heading"),
            rule_based_only=True,
        )
        cl["clause_types"] = result.labels
        cl["classification_confidence"] = result.confidence
        cl["classification_method"] = result.method
    return clauses


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Evaluation harness
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def evaluate_against_csv(
    csv_path: Path,
    *,
    sample_size: Optional[int] = None,
) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """Compute precision/recall/F1 of our rule-based classifier on a held-out CSV.

    Expects columns: text, category.
    """
    import csv as _csv
    import random

    _csv.field_size_limit(2**31 - 1)

    rows: List[dict] = []
    with Path(csv_path).open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        rows = list(_csv.DictReader(fh))
    if sample_size:
        random.seed(42)
        rows = random.sample(rows, min(sample_size, len(rows)))

    tp = 0
    fp = 0
    fn = 0
    for row in rows:
        text = (row.get("text") or "").strip()
        gold = row.get("category", "").strip()
        if not text or not gold:
            continue
        pred = set(classify_clause(text).labels)
        if not pred:
            pred = {"Miscellaneous"}
        gold_set = {gold}
        tp += len(pred & gold_set)
        fp += len(pred - gold_set)
        fn += len(gold_set - pred)
    precision = tp / max(1, tp + fp)
    recall = tp / max(1, tp + fn)
    f1 = 2 * precision * recall / max(1, precision + recall)
    return {
        "rows": len(rows),
        "tp": tp,
        "fp": fp,
        "fn": fn,
        "precision": round(precision, 4),
        "recall": round(recall, 4),
        "f1": round(f1, 4),
    }


// File: nlp/clause_classification/tfidf_model.py (python)
"""Runtime loader for the bundled TF-IDF clause classifier.

The repository ships the model compressed as ``models/tfidf_classifier.7z``
because the raw joblib is ~100 MB. We extract it on first use, so a plain
``pip install`` of the project has a working classifier without requiring a
7-Zip executable on PATH.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import warnings
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Optional

import joblib  # type: ignore

from nlp.taxonomy import INTERNAL_LABELS

MODEL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "models"
ARCHIVE_PATH = MODEL_DIR / "tfidf_classifier.7z"
MODEL_PATH = MODEL_DIR / "tfidf_classifier.joblib"

MODEL_LABEL_ALIASES = {"Pricing Terms": "Payment Terms"}
_CANONICAL_LABELS = frozenset(INTERNAL_LABELS)


def canonical_label(label: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Map a legacy model label into the canonical taxonomy, or drop it."""
    mapped = MODEL_LABEL_ALIASES.get(label, label)
    return mapped if mapped in _CANONICAL_LABELS else None


@dataclass
class TrainedClassifier:
    pipeline: object
    labels: List[str]

    def predict_one(self, text: str) -> List[str]:
        if not text:
            return []
        proba = self.pipeline.predict_proba([text])[0]
        classes = list(self.pipeline.classes_)
        ranked = sorted(zip(classes, proba, strict=False), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])
        out: List[str] = []
        for label, p in ranked:
            if p < 0.15:
                continue
            label = canonical_label(label)
            if label and label not in out:
                out.append(label)
            if len(out) >= 5:
                break
        if out:
            return out
        if ranked:
            top = canonical_label(ranked[0][0])
            return [top] if top else []
        return []

    def predict_top1(self, text: str) -> str:
        if not text:
            return "Miscellaneous"
        label = canonical_label(self.pipeline.predict([text])[0])
        return label or "Miscellaneous"


def ensure_model_file() -> Optional[Path]:
    """Return the extracted joblib path, extracting the archive if needed."""
    if MODEL_PATH.exists():
        return MODEL_PATH
    if not ARCHIVE_PATH.exists():
        return None
    try:
        import py7zr  # type: ignore

        with py7zr.SevenZipFile(ARCHIVE_PATH, mode="r") as archive:
            members = archive.getnames()
            target = next((n for n in members if n.endswith("tfidf_classifier.joblib")), None)
            if target is None:
                return None
            archive.extract(path=MODEL_DIR, targets=[target])
        extracted = MODEL_DIR / target
        if extracted != MODEL_PATH and extracted.exists():
            extracted.replace(MODEL_PATH)
    except Exception:
        return None
    return MODEL_PATH if MODEL_PATH.exists() else None


def _suppress_version_warning():
    try:
        from sklearn.exceptions import InconsistentVersionWarning

        warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=InconsistentVersionWarning)
    except Exception:
        pass


def load_trained(model_path: Optional[Path] = None) -> Optional[TrainedClassifier]:
    model_path = Path(model_path) if model_path else ensure_model_file()
    if model_path is None or not model_path.exists():
        return None
    _suppress_version_warning()
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        blob = joblib.load(model_path)
    if isinstance(blob, dict):
        return TrainedClassifier(pipeline=blob["pipeline"], labels=blob["labels"])
    return TrainedClassifier(pipeline=blob.pipeline, labels=blob.labels)


// File: nlp/ner/ner_ml.py (python)
"""DeBERTa-v3 NER enrichment wrapper. Loaded lazily."""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List

from app.models.schemas import Entity

try:  # pragma: no cover - optional import
    from transformers import AutoModelForTokenClassification, AutoTokenizer  # type: ignore
    _TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE = True
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
    _TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE = False


_MODEL = None
_TOKENIZER = None


def _load_model():  # pragma: no cover
    global _MODEL, _TOKENIZER
    if _MODEL is not None:
        return
    from app.core.config import get_settings

    settings = get_settings()
    model_name = settings.ner_model
    _TOKENIZER = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir=settings.hf_home)
    _MODEL = AutoModelForTokenClassification.from_pretrained(
        model_name, cache_dir=settings.hf_home, ignore_mismatched_sizes=True,
    )
    _MODEL.eval()


def enrich_entities_with_deberta(text: str, *, existing: List[Entity]) -> List[Entity]:
    """Append PARTY/ORG/DATE entities that regex missed. Best-effort."""
    if not _TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE or not text or not text.strip():
        return existing
    try:
        _load_model()
    except Exception:
        return existing

    try:  # pragma: no cover
        import torch
        tokens = _TOKENIZER(
            text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512, padding=True,
        )
        with torch.no_grad():
            logits = _MODEL(**tokens).logits
        predictions = torch.argmax(logits, dim=-1)[0].cpu().tolist()
        id2label = _MODEL.config.id2label
        offsets = _TOKENIZER(
            text, return_offsets_mapping=True, truncation=True, max_length=512,
        )["offset_mapping"][0]
        seen = {(e.label, e.text.lower()) for e in existing}
        for pred, (start, end) in zip(predictions, offsets, strict=False):
            if start == end:
                continue
            label = id2label.get(pred, "O")
            if not label or label == "O":
                continue
            value = label.split("-")[-1]
            if value not in {"PARTY", "ORG", "DATE"}:
                continue
            span = text[start:end]
            key = (value, span.lower())
            if key in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            existing.append(
                Entity(
                    text=span,
                    label=value,
                    start_char=start,
                    end_char=end,
                    confidence=0.75,
                    source="ner",
                )
            )
    except Exception:
        return existing
    return existing

"""Named Entity Recognition for legal contracts.

The MVP is regex-first because:
  * Indian identifiers (CIN/PAN/GSTIN) have deterministic formats.
  * The heavy NER model (DeBERTa) is optional and degrades gracefully.
  * Regex matches give us high precision on dates, amounts, and notice periods.

When the DeBERTa model is available, `extract_entities_with_deberta` enriches
the result with general entities (PARTY, ORG, DATE) where regex missed.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

from app.models.schemas import Entity
from app.utils.text import clean_text

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Regex patterns
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# CIN: 21 characters, e.g. U63040MH2019PTC123456.
CIN_RE = re.compile(r"\b[LUFE]\d{5}[A-Z]{2}\d{4}[A-Z]{3}\d{6}\b")
LLPIN_RE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}\b")
PAN_RE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z]{5}\d{4}[A-Z]\b")
GSTIN_RE = re.compile(r"\b\d{2}[A-Z]{5}\d{4}[A-Z][0-9A-Z]Z[0-9A-Z]\b")
TAN_RE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z]{4}\d{5}[A-Z]\b")

# Indian cities (abbreviated — covers top commercial centres)
INDIAN_CITIES = {
    "mumbai", "delhi", "new delhi", "bengaluru", "bangalore", "chennai",
    "kolkata", "hyderabad", "pune", "ahmedabad", "jaipur", "lucknow",
    "kanpur", "nagpur", "indore", "thane", "bhopal", "visakhapatnam",
    "patna", "vadodara", "ghaziabad", "ludhiana", "agra", "nashik",
    "faridabad", "meerut", "rajkot", "varanasi", "srinagar", "aurangabad",
    "dhanbad", "amritsar", "navi mumbai", "allahabad", "prayagraj",
    "guwahati", "chandigarh", "ranchi", "coimbatore", "mysuru", "mysore",
    "kochi", "trivandrum", "thiruvananthapuram", "gurugram", "gurgaon",
    "noida", "greater noida", "dehradun", "shimla", "manali",
}

INDIAN_STATES = {
    "andhra pradesh", "arunachal pradesh", "assam", "bihar", "chhattisgarh",
    "goa", "gujarat", "haryana", "himachal pradesh", "jharkhand", "karnataka",
    "kerala", "madhya pradesh", "maharashtra", "manipur", "meghalaya",
    "mizoram", "nagaland", "odisha", "orissa", "punjab", "rajasthan",
    "sikkim", "tamil nadu", "telangana", "tripura", "uttar pradesh",
    "uttarakhand", "west bengal", "delhi", "jammu and kashmir",
    "ladakh", "chandigarh", "puducherry",
}

# Foreign arbitration seats commonly seen in Indian cross-border contracts
FOREIGN_SEATS = {
    "singapore", "london", "hong kong", "dubai", "new york", "zurich",
    "paris", "geneva", "kuala lumpur", "shanghai", "tokyo", "frankfurt",
    "amsterdam", "stockholm", "vienna", "madrid", "rome", "seoul",
}

INDIAN_SEATS = {
    "new delhi", "mumbai", "bengaluru", "bangalore", "chennai", "kolkata",
    "hyderabad", "pune", "ahmedabad", "jaipur", "lucknow", "kochi",
    "guwahati", "chandigarh", "india",
}

INR_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:(?:Rs\.?|INR|₹)\s?[\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:crore|lakh|lac|crore[s]?|/-)?)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
USD_RE = re.compile(r"\$\s?[\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?(?:\s?(?:USD|US dollars?))?", re.IGNORECASE)
EUR_RE = re.compile(r"(?:€|EUR)\s?[\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?", re.IGNORECASE)
GBP_RE = re.compile(r"(?:£|GBP)\s?[\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?", re.IGNORECASE)

DATE_RES = [
    re.compile(r"\b\d{1,2}\s+(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)\s+\d{4}\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)\s+\d{1,2},?\s+\d{4}\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{2,4}\b"),
    re.compile(r"\b\d{1,2}-\d{1,2}-\d{2,4}\b"),
    re.compile(r"\bFY\s?\d{4}-?\d{0,4}", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b\d{1,2}\s?(?:st|nd|rd|th)?\s+(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    # Abbreviated month forms: "07 Jan 2025", "Jan 7, 2025"
    re.compile(r"\b\d{1,2}\s+(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)\s+\d{2,4}\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)\s+\d{1,2},?\s+\d{4}\b", re.IGNORECASE),
]
NOTICE_PERIOD_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:within|no later than|at least|prior to|after)?\s*(\d+)\s+"
    r"(hour|hours|day|days|week|weeks|month|months|year|years|business day[s]?)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
TERM_DURATION_RE = re.compile(
    r"\bfor a (?:period|term) of\s+(\d+)\s+"
    r"(day|days|week|weeks|month|months|year|years)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
CURE_PERIOD_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:cure period|to cure|within)\s+(\d+)\s+"
    r"(day|days|week|weeks|month|months)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data classes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass
class ExtractionResult:
    entities: List[Entity]
    methods: Dict[str, str]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public API
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def extract_entities(text: str, *, clause_text: Optional[str] = None) -> ExtractionResult:
    """Extract entities from clause text using regex rules.

    Returns a list of Entity objects with char offsets relative to the
    supplied text. Falls back to the contract-wide text if clause-level
    text isn't useful.
    """
    scan_text = clause_text or text or ""
    entities: List[Entity] = []

    # Indian identifiers
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(CIN_RE, scan_text, "CIN", 0.99))
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(LLPIN_RE, scan_text, "LLPIN", 0.95))
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(PAN_RE, scan_text, "PAN", 0.99))
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(GSTIN_RE, scan_text, "GSTIN", 0.99))
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(TAN_RE, scan_text, "TAN", 0.95))

    # Money
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(INR_RE, scan_text, "PAYMENT_AMOUNT", 0.95))
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(USD_RE, scan_text, "PAYMENT_AMOUNT", 0.95))
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(EUR_RE, scan_text, "PAYMENT_AMOUNT", 0.95))
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(GBP_RE, scan_text, "PAYMENT_AMOUNT", 0.95))

    # Dates
    for regex in DATE_RES:
        entities.extend(_scan_regex(regex, scan_text, "DATE", 0.95))

    # Notice / term durations
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(NOTICE_PERIOD_RE, scan_text, "NOTICE_PERIOD", 0.9))
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(TERM_DURATION_RE, scan_text, "TERM_DURATION", 0.9))
    entities.extend(_scan_regex(CURE_PERIOD_RE, scan_text, "CURE_PERIOD", 0.9))

    # Locations (jurisdictions / cities / seats)
    entities.extend(_scan_locations(scan_text))

    # DeBERTa NER enrichment (optional)
    try:
        from nlp.ner.ner_ml import enrich_entities_with_deberta

        enriched = enrich_entities_with_deberta(scan_text, existing=entities)
        entities = enriched
    except Exception:
        pass

    # Dedup
    seen = set()
    deduped: List[Entity] = []
    for e in entities:
        key = (e.label, e.text.lower(), e.start_char)
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        deduped.append(e)
    return ExtractionResult(entities=deduped, methods={"primary": "regex"})


def detect_arbitration_seat(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Return the most likely arbitration seat mentioned in text.

    Heuristic:
      1. Prefer explicit phrases: "seat of arbitration shall be X".
      2. Inside arbitration-context sentences, prefer FOREIGN seats, then
         Indian *cities* (not the generic "India").
      3. Skip the generic "India" entry unless nothing more specific was found.
    """
    cleaned = clean_text(text)
    lowered = cleaned.lower()

    # 1. Explicit phrase
    explicit = re.search(
        r"seat\s+of\s+arbitration\s+(?:shall\s+be|is|means)\s+([A-Za-z][A-Za-z\s,]{2,60})",
        lowered,
    )
    if explicit:
        raw = explicit.group(1)
        known = sorted(FOREIGN_SEATS | (INDIAN_SEATS - {"india"}), key=len, reverse=True)
        for seat in known:
            if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(seat)}\b", raw):
                return seat.title()
        value = re.split(r"\b(?:and|or)\b|[.;]", raw, maxsplit=1)[0].strip().rstrip(",.")
        if value and value.lower() not in {"india", "indian"}:
            return value.title()

    # 2. Walk arbitration-context sentences and prefer specific cities
    for sent in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", cleaned):
        ls = sent.lower()
        if "arbitration" not in ls and "seat" not in ls and "venue" not in ls:
            continue
        for seat in FOREIGN_SEATS:
            if seat in ls:
                return seat.title()
        for seat in INDIAN_SEATS - {"india"}:
            if seat in ls:
                return seat.title()

    # 3. Anywhere — first foreign seat, then specific Indian city.
    for seat in FOREIGN_SEATS:
        if seat in lowered:
            return seat.title()
    for seat in INDIAN_SEATS - {"india"}:
        if seat in lowered:
            return seat.title()

    # 4. Last resort — return "India" only as generic jurisdiction.
    if "india" in lowered or "indian" in lowered:
        return "India"
    return None


def detect_arbitration_venue(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Return the arbitration venue if explicitly stated, else ``None``."""
    cleaned = clean_text(text)
    m = re.search(
        r"(?:venue|place)\s+of\s+arbitration\s+(?:shall\s+be|is|at)\s+([A-Za-z][A-Za-z\s,]{2,60})",
        cleaned,
        re.IGNORECASE,
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    raw = m.group(1)
    known = sorted(FOREIGN_SEATS | (INDIAN_SEATS - {"india"}), key=len, reverse=True)
    for seat in known:
        if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(seat)}\b", raw, re.IGNORECASE):
            return seat.title()
    return raw.split(".")[0].strip().rstrip(",.").title() or None


def detect_governing_law(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Return the governing law phrase if found, preserving source casing."""
    cleaned = clean_text(text)
    patterns = [
        r"governed by the laws of[^.]{0,80}",
        r"governing law[^.]{0,80}laws of[^.]{0,80}",
        r"subject to the laws of[^.]{0,80}",
        r"laws of the state of[^.]{0,80}",
        r"laws of india",
    ]
    for pat in patterns:
        m = re.search(pat, cleaned, re.IGNORECASE)
        if m:
            phrase = m.group(0).strip().rstrip(".,")
            return phrase[:160]
    return None


def detect_stamp_duty_mention(text: str) -> bool:
    lowered = clean_text(text).lower()
    return any(kw in lowered for kw in ("stamp duty", "e-stamp", "franking", "indian stamp act"))


def detect_tds_mention(text: str) -> bool:
    lowered = clean_text(text).lower()
    return bool(re.search(r"\b(?:tax deducted at source|tds|section 19[45])\b", lowered))


def detect_gstin_mention(text: str) -> bool:
    return bool(GSTIN_RE.search(clean_text(text)))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Internals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _scan_locations(text: str) -> List[Entity]:
    """Match city/state/seat names, preferring longer names over substrings."""
    lowered = text.lower()
    groups = (
        ("JURISDICTION_CITY", INDIAN_CITIES, 0.9),
        ("INDIAN_STATE", INDIAN_STATES, 0.9),
        ("ARBITRATION_SEAT_INDIA", INDIAN_SEATS, 0.85),
        ("ARBITRATION_SEAT_FOREIGN", FOREIGN_SEATS, 0.85),
    )
    entities: List[Entity] = []
    for label, names, confidence in groups:
        taken: List[tuple[int, int]] = []
        for name in sorted(names, key=len, reverse=True):
            for m in re.finditer(rf"\b{re.escape(name)}\b", lowered):
                if any(m.start() < end and m.end() > start for start, end in taken):
                    continue
                if len(taken) >= 25:
                    break
                taken.append((m.start(), m.end()))
                entities.append(
                    Entity(
                        text=text[m.start() : m.end()],
                        label=label,
                        start_char=m.start(),
                        end_char=m.end(),
                        confidence=confidence,
                        source="regex",
                    )
                )
    return entities


def _scan_regex(pattern: re.Pattern, text: str, label: str, confidence: float) -> List[Entity]:
    matches: List[Entity] = []
    for m in pattern.finditer(text):
        matches.append(
            Entity(
                text=m.group(0),
                label=label,
                start_char=m.start(),
                end_char=m.end(),
                confidence=confidence,
                source="regex",
            )
        )
    return matches


// File: nlp/taxonomy.py (python)
"""Canonical clause taxonomy shared by dataset loaders and the classifier.

Keeping a single source of truth prevents the drift where the same CUAD or
MAUD label mapped to different internal categories in different modules.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Optional

# These MUST stay in sync with nlp.clause_classification.classifier.CLAUSE_RULES.
INTERNAL_LABELS = (
    "Payment Terms",
    "Term and Renewal",
    "Termination",
    "Indemnification",
    "Limitation of Liability",
    "Warranty",
    "Confidentiality",
    "Data Protection",
    "Intellectual Property",
    "Non-Compete / Non-Solicit",
    "Governing Law",
    "Dispute Resolution",
    "Force Majeure",
    "Assignment",
    "Audit Rights",
    "Insurance",
    "Compliance",
    "Service Levels",
    "Change Control",
    "Notice",
    "Acceptance",
    "Definitions",
    "Miscellaneous",
    "Stamp Duty",
    "TDS / GST",
    "Arbitration Seat",
)

# All 41 CUAD categories.
CUAD_TO_INTERNAL = {
    "Document Name": "Definitions",
    "Parties": "Definitions",
    "Agreement Date": "Definitions",
    "Effective Date": "Term and Renewal",
    "Expiration Date": "Term and Renewal",

def _map(label: str, mapping: dict[str, str]) -> Optional[str]:
    label = (label or "").strip()
    if label in mapping:
        return mapping[label]
    lowered = {k.lower(): v for k, v in mapping.items()}
    return lowered.get(label.lower())


def map_cuad_label(label: str) -> Optional[str]:
    return _map(label, CUAD_TO_INTERNAL)


def map_maud_label(label: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Map a MAUD text_type, or fall back to a coarse question hint."""
    mapped = _map(label, MAUD_TEXT_TYPE_TO_INTERNAL)
    if mapped:
        return mapped
    lowered = (label or "").lower()
    for needle, target in MAUD_QUESTION_HINTS.items():
        if needle in lowered:
            return target
    return None
